rationale: Base44 offers a documented SDK for programmatic CRUD on entities, a CLI for creating/syncing/deploying apps, and MCP server support for external AI assistants to interact with published apps, matching AI-native programmatic app generation and management. No formal REST/OpenAPI spec was found, but SDK/CLI/MCP together provide substantive programmatic control.

A probe confirms llms.txt is live at docs.base44.com/llms.txt returning HTTP 200 with structured agent-oriented documentation summary, and Base44 also explicitly supports bringing your own AI coding agent to interact with app docs/code and sandbox, plus .md doc endpoints throughout.

Base44's 'AI agents' feature lets AI chat-based agents read and act on app data (update records, trigger workflows) which could surface some data-driven suggestions, but there is no explicit evidence of dedicated AI-generated insights, analytics, or recommendation dashboards over user data.

Base44's docs mention AI agents that can 'trigger workflows' and 'connect to tools' from chat interactions, suggesting some agentic action-taking, but there's no clear evidence of scheduled or event-driven automations running autonomously in the background without a user prompt.

Base44's core interaction model is delegating app-building tasks to an AI assistant that generates designs, code, and content from natural-language prompts (docs-12,14,21; probe-1), and community testimonials confirm the AI assistant reliably executes substantial tasks like full app builds from prompts (comm-4,5,6), though some users note it's essentially an LLM wrapper (comm-1) and cost/quality tradeoffs (comm-8).

Base44 exposes a CLI (create, login, deploy) and an SDK for CRUD operations, which could in principle be scripted, but there is no documented support for non-interactive auth, API tokens, or CI-specific workflows—'login' implies interactive auth, and no CI/automation guide or headless mode is mentioned.

Base44 documents an 'App MCP' feature that exposes its own app as an MCP server for external assistants like Claude/ChatGPT to connect to (docs-7), which is the reverse of the story — there's no evidence Base44 itself can consume/plug in external MCP servers to gain their tools.

Base44 documents an official 'App MCP' feature that exposes a published app as its own Model Context Protocol server, explicitly enabling external AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor to connect as agents.

Base44's core product is natural-language app building — describing ideas in chat to generate full-stack apps, design changes, and data operations — corroborated by docs (AI agents, design previews, board for sending instructions to AI) and strong community testimony that prompting alone produces functional apps ('two prompts and deploy', 'far superior' output).

Base44 documents an official CLI (installable via npm) that supports login, create, sync, deploy, and eject commands, with clear docs and getting-started guides confirming it is a first-party tool for building/managing apps from the terminal.

Base44 documents a JS SDK (entities CRUD, auth), a CLI, and an App MCP server letting external AI assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor) interact with published apps, all backed by concrete code samples — a real, documented programmatic surface for AI-native use. However, no formal OpenAPI/REST spec exists (probe found 404s on all candidate openapi.json paths), so the 'public API' is SDK/CLI/MCP-based rather than a conventional documented REST API.

There is no evidence of scoped or least-privilege API credentials/keys for agents; docs mention login/authentication for CLI ('base44 login') and SDK usage but no mention of API key scopes, permission levels, or credential restriction. A security incident report even shows app_id alone granted broad access, suggesting weak access controls rather than fine-grained scoping.

Base44 provides an official SDK with documented entities/CRUD methods, a CLI for creating/managing projects, and code examples for building against the backend, showing genuine SDK support (base44-docs-4, -17, -23, -28, -24). However, there's no OpenAPI spec (base44-probe-2 shows 404s), and community commentary frames Base44 primarily as an AI-driven no-code/low-code builder rather than a mature developer SDK ecosystem, suggesting the SDK is functional but secondary to the AI-first workflow.

No evidence pack items mention webhooks or event subscription capabilities; the SDK docs cover CRUD entities and MCP/agent integrations but nothing about outbound event notifications or webhook subscriptions.

Base44 provides SDK reference docs with code snippets (e.g., entity CRUD examples) and CLI documentation, but there is no evidence of an interactive, runnable API explorer—probes for OpenAPI/Swagger endpoints all returned 404, indicating no live interactive reference exists.

Direct probes for OpenAPI/swagger spec endpoints all returned 404, and no documentation page mentions a downloadable OpenAPI or machine-readable API spec; only an SDK and CLI are documented, not a formal spec file.

Evidence shows local development, ejecting/cloning apps, and BYO-agent sandbox connections, but nothing describes a dedicated sandbox/staging environment isolated from production data for testing purposes. There's no mention of environment separation, test data, or non-production data safety guarantees.

There's SDK/CLI documentation but no evidence of API versioning scheme or a documented deprecation policy; openapi.json probes returned 404, and no docs mention version numbers or deprecation timelines.

Base44 docs describe built-in AI agents that can act within apps and an MCP server to connect external AI assistants, implying managed AI integration without exposing provider keys, but there's no explicit documentation confirming key management is abstracted away for LLM calls added by the user.

No documentation or feature describes an automated security review/scan of generated apps before publishing. In fact, community evidence describes a real vulnerability found by an outside researcher (not caught by the platform) and criticism that code was pushed without reviews, undermining any claim of built-in security vetting.

Base44 docs confirm built-in, customizable login/register/forgot-password pages generated automatically for every app, with support for multiple sign-up methods (email, Google, other providers) and in-app branding/design customization — directly matching the scaffolded auth story.

The SDK docs show only single-record CRUD operations (e.g., entities.Task.create for one item) with no mention of batch/bulk create, update, or delete APIs, and no other evidence pack item references bulk operations across many items.

Base44 docs mention AI agents that 'trigger workflows' and 'update records' from chat interactions, suggesting some automation-on-action capability, but there's no evidence of a declarative event-based rule engine (e.g., 'when X happens, do Y') distinct from conversational agent triggers.

No evidence of any scheduling, cron, or recurring workflow trigger capability in Base44's docs; AI agents and workflows are triggered by chat/actions, not time-based schedules, and no mention of scheduled jobs appears anywhere in the evidence pack.

Base44 offers GitHub sync for general code version control (docs-2, docs-18) which could theoretically let users track and revert changes to automation logic, but there's no dedicated feature for versioning, reviewing, or rolling back specific 'automations' (e.g., AI agents/workflows) within the platform itself. Community commentary even notes the founder pushed code daily without code reviews, undermining confidence in a built-in review/rollback discipline.

Base44's docs explicitly cover connecting a custom domain, including automatic SSL certificate issuance/renewal once the domain is connected, indicating a supported end-to-end flow for founders to attach their own domain to a published app.

Base44 provides an 'eject' CLI command to download frontend and backend resources locally and a SDK to build custom frontends/backends against Base44 as a service, plus GitHub sync for local dev — but the exported project still relies on a new Base44 app ID and managed backend rather than fully independent deployment to arbitrary external infrastructure.

Base44's documented workflow is to eject/clone code out to a local project (via CLI or GitHub sync) or connect external agents to a sandbox—there's no evidence of an in-builder code editor where developers can view and edit generated source directly inside Base44's UI.

Base44 provides an explicit 'eject' CLI command that downloads full frontend and backend code into a new standalone project, plus GitHub sync and SDK access, supporting code export and local development. However, the ejected app still depends on Base44's own new app ID/backend, and there's no documented path to fully host/run independent of Base44's managed backend, so true platform-independent hosting is uncertain.

Base44 explicitly documents 'Bring your own AI coding agent, or your own scripts' by connecting to the app's sandbox, plus GitHub sync for local development and a CLI/SDK that exposes the backend as code so external agents can drive the build. This directly supports connecting a third-party coding agent to work alongside or instead of the built-in one, though depth of hands-on community validation is limited.

Base44 is built as a prompt-to-app tool that generates full-stack apps—frontend UI plus a managed backend with data entities, auth, and workflows—from natural language descriptions, confirmed by docs and community reports of one/two-prompt fully functional apps.

Base44 docs explicitly describe connecting an app to GitHub for two-way sync between local development and Base44's editor, enabling version control and collaboration, though no community evidence corroborates real-world reliability of this bidirectional sync.

Docs explicitly claim 'Turn a Figma frame into a working app' and starting from an existing website in the Quick-start guide, directly matching the story, but this is only a brief vendor claim with no independent community validation or detail on fidelity/import quality.

Base44 offers AI-driven design previews before changes are applied (base44-docs-14) and community praise for quick iteration with two-prompt builds (base44-comm-6), suggesting some safeguard against breaking existing work. However, other community feedback describes hitting walls and escalating costs when trying to get the AI to iterate further (base44-comm-8), and no explicit versioning/rollback mechanism for prompt-based edits is documented.

Base44 provides GitHub sync for local editing that stays in sync with the platform, a CLI to eject/clone apps into local projects with their own app ID, an SDK for building against the backend, and support for bringing your own AI agent/scripts via sandbox connection—covering local dev with own tooling and pushing changes back.

Base44 apps are inherently hosted and automatically get a live URL with custom domain support and auto SSL, and community comments confirm 'two prompts and deploy' simplicity, implying publishing is near one-step. However, there's no explicit doc evidence of a single 'publish' button/step described, and some evidence (custom domain setup) implies extra configuration for professional URLs.

Base44 offers an SDK/CLI for CRUD on entities and backend management (base44-docs-4,5,17,23,28), and even lets external AI assistants interact via an MCP server (base44-docs-7), but there is no discoverable OpenAPI spec (base44-probe-2) and core UI-only capabilities like AI-driven design generation, visual page editing, and templating (base44-docs-12,13,14,20) appear to have no programmatic equivalent, so full UI parity via API is not evidenced.

Base44 lets users eject an app (download frontend code and backend resources into a new project) and sync code via GitHub, giving some portability of code, but there's no explicit documentation of exporting user data (tables/records) in open formats like CSV/JSON — only a UI to view data, not export it.

Base44 is a closed, proprietary SaaS app builder; users can eject/export their own generated app code but there is no evidence of the platform's own source (the builder engine itself) being available under an open license.

Base44 is presented purely as a managed SaaS app builder with CLI/SDK/eject tools to export generated app code, but there is no evidence anywhere of a self-hosted deployment of the core Base44 platform itself; eject creates a new project still tied to a Base44 app ID rather than an independent, self-runnable core product.

Marketing copy states the AI 'shows previews before it touches anything' and lets users 'see every page at once' while chatting to the AI, implying an interactive live preview during building, but there is no detailed documentation of a dedicated live-preview mode or hands-on community confirmation of this specific workflow.

No evidence in the pack mentions data residency, region selection, or storage location controls for Base44 apps; there's even a security vulnerability report about app data exposure but nothing on choosing storage regions.

No evidence in the pack addresses AI training data opt-out or privacy controls over user data usage for model training; documentation focuses on app-building features, SDK, CLI, and community discussions of security vulnerabilities, not data privacy/training policies.

No evidence in the pack addresses data retention policies, export, or deletion controls; documentation covers app building, CLI, SDK, and login features but nothing about managing or deleting stored data at the account/privacy level.

No evidence in the pack mentions telemetry, usage tracking, or any opt-out/privacy controls for Base44; documentation and community items cover unrelated features like CLI, SDK, security vulnerabilities, and app building.

Base44's core product is exactly this: natural-language prompts generate a full-stack app with managed backend, database, auth, and CLI/SDK access (docs-9,11,17,24,29). Community testimonials corroborate that prompting produces genuinely functional full apps, not just prototypes (e.g., 'Base44 provided me with a fully functional app', 'two prompts and deploy'), despite some skepticism about differentiation and cost.

Base44 provides a built-in managed database ('Data page' with tables/entities) automatically wired into apps without external setup, confirmed by docs on data management and SDK CRUD operations, and corroborated by a community comment praising the integrated DB as a key differentiator.

Base44 supports GitHub sync for code collaboration and has an app 'collaborator/editor' role (revealed via a security report), but there's no direct documentation of a true shared team workspace, roles/permissions, or multi-user project management features.

Base44 provides a real backend (entities/CRUD via SDK, CLI, custom backend code, AI agents that can 'connect to tools') and login pages with email-based auth, showing some server-side and integration capability, but the evidence pack never mentions payment gateways or dedicated email-sending integrations being addable from the builder.

Base44 explicitly supports starting from community-created templates via its App templates gallery, and even lets users publish their own templates; the CLI also supports creating projects from available templates instead of a blank prompt.

Base44 offers a global theme editor for colors/fonts without prompts, but there's no evidence of a direct element-selection editor for text/style/layout—most editing (design options, page changes) is described as going through AI prompts and previews rather than direct manipulation.

No pricing or documentation evidence explains how credits/tokens are consumed per action or what a plan includes; the only related evidence is a community complaint that billing is opaque and can run up unexpected costs, but no vendor-tier source substantiates or clarifies token usage.

However, several UI-only workflows—GitHub branch/PR management, CI fix/conflict resolution, visual style editing, command palette—have no documented API equivalents in the evidence pack, so full parity is unverified.

v0 lets users push generated code to GitHub and import/export code freely (v0-docs-2, v0-docs-31, v0-docs-37), which supports leaving with the core generated-code artifact in an open format. However, there's no evidence of exporting full account data—chat histories, project metadata, settings—in open formats, so a user could not fully 'export all data and leave'.

v0 is a closed, proprietary SaaS product; there is no evidence of an open-source license for its core source code. The v0-sdk GitHub repo is just a client SDK wrapper, not the product's source itself.

v0 is exclusively offered as a hosted SaaS product (Vercel-powered deployments, credit-based pricing, cloud API); there is no evidence anywhere in the pack of a self-hostable core product, open-source release, or on-prem deployment option.

v0's core product experience is a chat interface paired with a live, interactive preview pane where founders can fine-tune UI details before deploying or publishing via GitHub/Vercel; docs explicitly describe 'live preview' and 'preview deployments from working branches' plus community reports confirm the iterate-then-deploy workflow.
No evidence in the pack mentions data residency, region selection, or storage location controls for v0.
The evidence pack contains no mention of data-training opt-out, privacy controls, or AI training policies for v0; nothing addresses whether user data/chats are used to train models or how to opt out.

The evidence pack contains no mention of data retention controls, deletion options, privacy settings, or data policies for v0; nothing addresses how user chats, projects, or generated code can be retained or deleted.
No evidence in the pack mentions telemetry, usage tracking, analytics opt-out, or privacy controls for v0.

v0's docs explicitly describe scaffolding full-stack apps, connecting to backends/databases, and one-click deployment, and community evidence confirms a founder built a working, feature-rich MVP (auth, roles, export) from prompt to deployed app in a day.

v0 docs describe Project-level integrations with databases like Neon (Postgres) and Upstash (Redis) plus Supabase, and claim v0 'connects to databases as it builds,' suggesting in-builder wiring. However, this appears to be connecting to externally-provisioned services rather than full in-app database provisioning, and no hands-on community evidence confirms a seamless zero-leave experience.

v0 Projects let multiple chats share deployment, hosting, and environment variables (v0-docs-11, v0-docs-21, v0-docs-29), and a Business plan exists (v0-docs-23), suggesting some team-oriented infrastructure. However, there's no explicit evidence of multi-user access controls, invites, or real-time collaborative editing within a shared workspace.

v0 docs confirm connecting projects to third-party services/backends (databases like Upstash/Neon, backend services like Supabase, AI providers) and building server-side/full-stack functionality, but no evidence specifically confirms built-in payments or email integrations from the builder.

v0 supports alternative starting points—importing existing GitHub repos, cloning pages from screenshots/Figma, and starting from existing files—which reduce the 'blank prompt' problem, but the evidence pack contains no explicit template gallery or community project marketplace like other tools offer.

v0's core workflow is prompt-driven chat generation; the only hint of direct manipulation is the vague marketing line 'Fine-tune every detail with visual controls and live preview,' with no docs or community evidence detailing an actual select-and-edit UI for text/style/layout.

Docs confirm plan tiers, ability to buy extra credits, and note that starting from existing files uses no tokens (docs-10, docs-23, docs-25), but there's no detailed breakdown of per-action token/credit costs. A community report describes unpredictable, high usage-based costs (>$20/day, $50 for a weekend project), contradicting a clear understanding of consumption (v0-comm-3).
